clips.title: The story
paras: Above Ratchet, Strahad Farsan sends an aspiring Alliance warlock to the Library of Ironforge. A felhunter’s hunger can overwhelm an unprepared summoner, and the Tome of the Cabal holds the knowledge needed to summon and bind the demon.

An imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus can be subdued through ritual, but a felhunter brings a different hazard. Felhunters serve the Burning Legion and hunt down arcane energy to devour it. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner’s magic before a binding can take hold. From his redoubt in the Barrens, Strahad Farsan watches over Ratchet and knows an amateur must not attempt the binding unprepared.

An acolyte needs the arcane formulas in the Tome of the Cabal to draw forth and bind a felhunter safely. The earliest mortal cabal of warlocks who successfully broke a felhunter without outside aid authored the manuscript. Its pages detail the geomancy, materials, and binding runes needed to withstand the creature’s hunger. The copy was lost long ago, leaving Strahad and his circle without the masterwork.

Strahad sends Alliance warlocks across the Great Sea to the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, since he cannot provide the text himself. Krom Stoutarm, an itinerant dwarven warlock, resides there and spends his twilight years combing through ancient manuscripts and library records. If any trace of the lost grimoire remains recorded in the Eastern Kingdoms, it rests buried in Krom’s meticulous catalogs.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: It will take more than a simple summoning circle to bring forth a felhunter for you to challenge.

My three acolytes and I will assist in creating the magic circles. You require a copy of the Tome of the Cabal, which has been lost to us for some time. It was written by the first group of warlocks to summon a felhunter unaided.
Perhaps Krom Stoutarm can help you with this. An itinerant warlock these days, he spends his days hoarding ancient texts and skulking about the library in Ironforge.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Tome of the Cabal? Hmm... Sounds familiar. I've never seen it here before, though—and believe me, I remember every book I read.
Ah, yes! I have seen references to it in library cataloguing books.
